page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical AMD EPYC 7B13 core using x86_64 architecture. The server has a dedicated CPU allocation running 2 threads per core, 4.0 GB of system memory, and a 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI for cryptographic and vector processing. This configuration includes no attached local storage, no discrete GPUs, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c2d-highcpu-2 displays strong single-core CPU results in stress-ng tests, ranking in the top 25 percentile with a score of 2921.98. However, multi-core CPU throughput, memory bandwidth, and database performance metrics fall into lower percentiles due to the 2 vCPU and 4.0 GB RAM footprint. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 31.59 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput reaches 2.82 GB/sec. Small language model text generation achieves 77.68 tokens/sec using a 135M parameter model.

The resource profile provides efficient single-threaded compute relative to its resource allocation, though total system capacity is constrained by memory size and core count. It is suited for light single-threaded execution, basic web serving, small utility scripts, and low-concurrency microservices.
